transcript: If you truly wish to taste sugar, my friend, a cookie, a donut, whatever temptation calls your name, there is a right moment to enjoy it with pleasure and a wrong moment that quietly harms the body. In the way of ancient healing, timing is everything. The best time to eat sugar is after a meal, as a dessert. Why? Because then your body is already protected. The fibers, proteins, and healthy fats from your meal form a shield, so the sugar enters slowly, gently, without causing chaos inside. But never eat sugar on an empty stomach, and never in the morning. Morning sugar is one of the great destroyers of balance. When you eat pastries for breakfast, the chocolate-filled croissant, the warm donut, the sweet bread, yes, it tastes beautiful, but it sends your body into war. The sugars break down instantly into glucose. They rush into the bloodstream, like soldiers without discipline, and you get a heavy glucose spike. About 90 minutes later, the crash comes, and now it is only 10 or 11 in the morning. Yet you already feel tired, unfocused, and hungry again. Your mind cries out, I need a cookie, I need chocolate, I need a snack. And just like that, the body becomes trapped in a cycle. Spike, crash, spike, crash. A rollercoaster that makes you feel addicted to sugar all day long. This is how modern people lose control, not from weakness, but from misunderstanding the ancient wisdom of timing. If you reached here, comment yes, and your country. And if you want to learn more ancient healing wisdom like this, the teachings are inside my ebook, Link in my Profile.
